title: Blank, missing or unreadable plan values silently become hard-coded household-specific dollar figures

evidence.description: Defaults applied when a value is blank or absent: annual_earned_income 290000, annual_spending_base_year 225000, mortgage monthly_payment 3000 (x12), balance_as_of_plan_start 293284 at interest_rate 0.0199 to last_payment_year 2034, home value 1313000, LTC face_value 250000, S-Corp reasonable_salary_annual 80000

_v returns the stored string, so a blank row gives ''. _n('' , default) passes the default into strict_float, which returns it for a blank cell. An unreadable value is only logged ('unparseable number ... using default') and the default is returned
A blank or None cell returns the supplied default, so the code default is used and nothing is raised
Start New Plan keeps every row but sets household facts to ''. The docstring itself says blanking 'drops the engine onto whatever hardcoded fallback happens to exist in code'
The default mortgage balance, rate and payment build mort_schedule and mort_interest_schedule
A positive default mort_pmt makes the mortgage payment count as a spending outflow up to mort_end
Default-derived mortgage interest feeds the itemized-deduction calculation
The schema has a blank default for mortgage balance (not required) and the other fields, and a 60000 default for reasonable_salary_annual. The parser uses 80000, so schema and parser disagree
The other config path defaults home_value to 0 and roth_brk to 0.24, so the two loaders give different results for the same missing value
Blank required fields are reported as preflight 'blockers', but only fields with required=TRUE. The mortgage fields are not required, so a blank mortgage is never flagged
/api/build/start does not check preflight blockers before it starts the build subprocess

observed_behavior: On the CSV/plan-row config path, a blank, missing or unreadable value in these fields is replaced with a specific dollar figure. These figures do not look generic (for example $293,284 mortgage balance at 1.99% through 2034, $3,000/month payment, $1,313,000 home, $290,000 earned income, $225,000 spending). Start New Plan creates exactly this state, because it blanks the rows instead of deleting them. A household with no mortgage that leaves the mortgage rows blank is projected to have a $293,284 mortgage with $36,000/yr payments and deductible interest. Nothing tells the user, because the mortgage fields are not marked required.
impact: Net worth, cash flow, itemized deductions, Roth sizing and survivor/insurance need (sheets_protection.py reads mort_bal) can be materially wrong for new plans or partly completed plans, and the output looks plausible. The same blank field also gives different values on the CSV and JSON config paths.
affected_workflows: Households with no mortgage, no home, or no earned income that leave fields blank
Typos in dollar fields (unreadable value, so the default is used)
root_cause: Code defaults in the CSV parser look like they were carried over from one real household's data, and the parser treats blank the same as 'use the code default' instead of 'none/zero'. Nothing enforces agreement between the schema default column and the parser defaults.
options: No credible alternative; this is a correctness defect.
recommendation: Make blank mean the schema default, or 0/none when the schema default is blank, for every dollar/rate field. Remove the household-specific literals from client_sections.py. Make an unreadable value a validation error, not a logged fallback. Add a contract test that parses a blank_plan_rows() plan and asserts mortgage balance, payment, home value, earned income and spending are zero or schema defaults. Add a test that each parser default equals the schema.csv default.
dependencies: QA-003 (dollars-type validation) so unreadable values are rejected before they reach the parser
implementation_considerations: Golden masters use fully populated fixtures, so they should not move. Confirm that with tools/regen_golden_master.py measure before any regeneration. The JSON/wizard path (data_io.py:858-885) should share the same default source.
risk_of_change: Low to medium. Plans that relied on the fallback without knowing it will change, so this needs a release note and a measure-first golden check.
verification_method: Static trace this run: blank_plan_rows -> '' -> _v -> _n -> strict_float default -> mort_schedule -> spending_and_rmd mort_yr. Confirm by a unit test that calls parse_client on a blanked frozen fixture and asserts c['mort_bal']==0 and c['home_val']==0.

In src/projection_stages/spending_and_rmd.py:336-338 a positive mort_pmt counts as a spending outflow up to mort_end, and src/projection_stages/roth_conversion_and_agi_tax.py:767 reads mort_interest_schedule. The JSON path in src/data_io.py (around 858) defaults home_value and mortgage_balance to 0, so the two loaders do disagree. No jurisdiction or rule-year question applies; this is not a tax-rule finding.

title: After Start New Plan, a grid save probably fails until every cleared required field is filled in the same save

evidence.description: After applying the posted updates, it runs _schema_validate_rows_full(store.all_rows()) on the whole plan. Any error rolls back every update and returns 422
Every row whose schema has required=TRUE and an empty value gets 'required value missing'

Clears household facts. Calling keeps_value() against reference_src/schema.csv (read-only import) shows 21 of 53 required fields are cleared, including member_1/2 name, dob, retirement_date, residence_state, filing_status, annual_earned_income, annual_spending_base_year and home value_as_of_plan_start
The UI saves through the validated grid endpoint
The client expects a 422 'Plan Data validation failed' and marks field errors
The test replaces /api/plan/blank with a mock, so the plan is never actually blanked and no save is tried afterward
Only the unvalidated /api/plan/forms path is tested after blanking, not /api/config/rows

observed_behavior: Every grid save checks the whole plan, and a blank plan has 21 empty required fields. So the first single-field save after Start New Plan should come back 422 with a list of 'required value missing' errors for fields the user has not reached yet. Single households also face required member_2 fields.
impact: If confirmed, new-plan creation is badly broken: users cannot save step by step and see a wall of errors. No test exercises this path, so it would not be caught.
root_cause: The save-time validation treats 'required' as a condition for saving at all, when it is really a condition for building. The new-plan tests mock or avoid the validated save path.
options: Check 'required' only at build/preflight time, and validate only type/range of changed rows on save
Validate the whole plan but downgrade 'required value missing' to warnings returned with a 200
Keep the current behaviour but have the blank plan carry neutral values (0, None) for required dollar fields; this conflicts with QA-001's goal of an explicit blank
recommendation: Option 1. Keep format/range checks on save, move 'required' to the build preflight (which already lists missing_required), and add a Python functional test: blank_plan_rows() then POST /api/config/rows with one field, expecting 200.
implementation_considerations: WI-020 field-level validation UI relies on field_errors from the 422. Keep that shape for format errors. Required-ness is also used by build_service preflight, which should become the gate that blocks builds.
risk_of_change: Low. This relaxes a save-time check and keeps the build-time one.
verification_method: Not run, because the review is static. Confirm with a test client: app_core._blank_plan_rows(), then POST /api/config/rows with one update, and check the status and errors list.
verification_rationale: The static chain is complete in files I opened. In src/server_services/config_service.py:518-545 the save applies the updates, runs _schema_validate_rows_full(store.all_rows()) on the whole plan (imported at line 19 as schema_registry.validate_rows), rolls back on any error and returns 422. src/schema_registry.py:16-19 adds 'required value missing' for any required=TRUE field that is empty, and validate_rows (lines 75-89) applies it to every row. blank_plan_rows clears the household rows, and schema.csv marks annual_earned_income, annual_spending_base_year and Home value_as_of_plan_start required=TRUE. The frontend saves only through /api/config/rows (dashboard.js:1095 and 5959, build_history.js:173); a grep found no frontend caller of /api/plan/forms. tests/test_blank_plan_rows_functional.py:71-78 tests only the forms path after blanking. I did not reproduce the '21 of 53' count myself, and the review is static, so I have not shown runtime behavior. I also cannot rule out that reference.db's schema differs from schema.csv. Confidence stays medium. If the finding holds, high severity fits, because the Start New Plan flow would be unusable.

title: Server checks numbers only for 'number' and 'currency', so the 114 'dollars' fields and the /api/plan/forms path accept text

evidence.description: Numeric format checks run only for typ in {'number','currency'} (and the finite check for integer/year/number/currency/percent/pct). 'dollars' and 'decimal' get no format check. The min/max check skips values that cannot be parsed
Type counts: percent 125, dollars 114, choice 92, date 66, year 41, text 40, boolean 30, integer 28, number 17, currency 11, decimal 2
Parametrized over number/currency/integer/percent only. The main money type, 'dollars', is not tested
/api/plan/forms POST/PATCH strips the value, normalizes Roth values and writes it with no schema validation
Downstream, an unreadable value is logged and replaced with the code default (see QA-001)

observed_behavior: A value like 'abc' or '12k' in a dollars field passes the grid save. On any write through /api/plan/forms nothing is validated. The parser then quietly uses the hard-coded default.
impact: Bad money input reaches the engine without the user knowing. The test suite's type list does not match the schema's, so the gap is invisible to the existing tests.
affected_workflows: Imports that land in plan rows
root_cause: The validator's type vocabulary was never matched to the schema's type vocabulary, and the two write paths have different validation contracts.
options: Treat 'dollars' and 'decimal' the same as 'currency' in validate_value, using money.is_strict_number
Make one shared row validator that both /api/config/rows and /api/plan/forms call
Both, plus a contract test that every type value in schema.csv is handled by validate_value
recommendation: Option 3. Normalize the type aliases, send forms writes through the same validator (format/range only, per QA-002), and add a test that fails when schema.csv contains a type validate_value does not handle.
dependencies: QA-002 (so that adding validation to forms does not bring the required-field blocker with it)
implementation_considerations: Use money.parse_strict_number as the one grammar, so the server, the parser and the client accept the same strings.
risk_of_change: Low to medium. Existing plans with bad dollar text will start failing validation on save, so a migration report helps.
verification_method: Static: compare the validate_value type sets with the schema.csv type counts. Confirm with validate_value('abc', {'type':'dollars'}) == [] before the fix.
verification_rationale: src/schema_registry.py:26-28 checks number format only for {'number','currency'}, and the finite-number check at 32 omits 'dollars' and 'decimal'. _numeric_value (lines 62-74) returns None for text it cannot parse, so the min/max check is skipped. I re-counted the type column of reference_src/schema.csv this run: dollars 114, decimal 2, number 17, currency 11, which matches the finding. The finding's list leaves out yes/no 3 and secret 2; this is minor. tests/test_plan_date_parsing_unit.py:98-103 parametrizes only over number, currency, integer and percent. src/server_services/plan_forms_service.py (_value, save/patch) only strips and normalizes Roth values, with no schema validation. One mitigation: the shipped frontend does not appear to call /api/plan/forms, so that half of the impact is limited to API and automation callers. The dollars gap in grid saves is real, and together with QA-001's silent default it lets bad money input through. Medium severity is appropriate.

title: API error objects from RetirementApiClient carry no HTTP status, so the build 404 fallback can never run

evidence.description: On !res.ok it throws Error(data.error||text) with err.errors and err.fieldErrors but no err.status. text() throws the raw response body
Sends every call through RetirementApiClient when it exists (index.html:98 loads it first). Only the unused inline fallback sets err.status, and that fallback does not set fieldErrors
The ARC-004 fallback depends on e.status === 404, which is never set, so it never fires
Covers only the negative case (no fallback after a job id). Nothing tests that a 404 triggers the fallback

observed_behavior: The two request paths throw errors of different shapes (status vs fieldErrors), and the main path never includes the HTTP status. /api/build/start is always registered (workbook_routes.py:196), so there is no user-visible failure today, but the documented fallback does not work.
impact: Little effect today. Any future code that branches on HTTP status will fail silently, and the ARC-004 fix looks done but is untested and does not work.
root_cause: The API client extraction (api_client.js) dropped err.status, and the remaining test checks only the behaviour that never needs it.
options: Set err.status = res.status in RetirementApiClient.request and delete the inline fallback in api()
Delete the 404 fallback branch as dead code
recommendation: Option 1, plus a frontend vm-sandbox or e2e test that returns 404 from /api/build/start and asserts POST /api/build is called.
implementation_considerations: Keep one error shape {message, status, errors, fieldErrors} and record it in API_CONTRACTS.md.
risk_of_change: Low.
verification_method: Static read of api_client.js:38-42 against build_lifecycle.js:258. A sandbox test with a mocked fetch returning 404.
verification_rationale: In frontend/js/api_client.js:38-42, request() builds the Error with errors and fieldErrors but never sets err.status. text() throws the raw body. In frontend/js/dashboard_decomp_row_model.js the api() function (around 4958-4960) sends every call through window.RetirementApiClient when it exists. frontend/index.html:98 loads api_client.js before row_model at line 108. Only the inline fallback, at about line 4988, sets err.status. frontend/js/dashboard_decomp_build_lifecycle.js:258 depends on e.status === 404, which the main path never sets, so the fallback is dead code. Severity stays low, since /api/build/start is registered and nothing breaks for users today. I did not open the e2e spec, but this does not change the verdict.

Workbook text points to reference_data/state_tax.csv

The actual source is reference_src/state_tax.csv, which is built into src/reference/reference.db. git ls-files shows 0 files under reference_data/

Point to reference_src/state_tax.csv plus tools/build_reference_db.py (only suitable for developers)

title: The frontend size ratchet keeps getting raised (100 of 106 changes), so it does not constrain size

evidence.description: Current ceiling is 43_777

100 of 106 changes raised the ceiling, for example 42,609->43,298 (61a9d7f2, #388), 43,298->43,620 (425fd97a, left-nav redesign), 43,762->43,818 (0bbfb472). The only notable cut is 2c293e62 to 43,777, done by removing blank lines
States 'Never raise it to pass'

observed_behavior: Feature commits raise the ceiling in the same change that adds UI. The guard counts lines but does not limit growth, and the one reduction came from removing blank lines.
impact: Gives false comfort about frontend growth. The guard costs effort on every UI change without enforcing what it is meant to enforce. Product behaviour is unaffected.
affected_workflows: Maintainability of large panel JS files
root_cause: The repo rule and the actual process disagree. Nothing requires a reason or an offsetting extraction when the ceiling is raised.
options: Require a matching extraction or deletion in the same commit (test compares with the previous ceiling and needs a recorded reason)
Replace the total-lines ceiling with per-file budgets for the largest modules
Drop the rule and record frontend size as a tracked metric, not a gate
recommendation: Option 2, or 1 with a required changelog line, so the rule in CLAUDE.md matches what is enforced.
implementation_considerations: Changing the guard is a test/tooling change only. Blank-line removal should not count as real reduction.
risk_of_change: Low.
verification_method: git log -p -- tests/test_frontend_size_ratchet.py, tallied by direction of change (done this run).
verification_rationale: TOTAL_JS_MAX_LINES = 43_777 is at tests/test_frontend_size_ratchet.py:695. Re-tallying git log -p this run gave 105 value changes, 100 raises and 5 cuts. The finding said 106, which is a negligible difference, and the direction holds. git show 2c293e62 confirms the cut came from removing 237 blank lines. A counterpoint: a ratchet that rises with real feature growth is not wrong in itself. Without a required reason or offsetting extraction, though, the gate does not enforce the project rule 'Never raise it to pass'. This is a process and governance issue with no product impact, so low severity is appropriate.
duplicate_rationale: Cross-expert duplicate (conflict C-01): same defect as ARC-005 (frontend size ceiling raised in feature work). The stronger finding is kept; this one's tally is folded in as corroborating evidence.
